LAUD 201.name: Design Studio I:Site Design
LAUD 201.description: The first stage of the Vertical Design Studio System composed of three different studios: Concept, Context and Form in which the second, third and fourth year students are enrolled. Basics of site design, i.e., understanding and analyzing the project area, characteristics, open space types in cities, landscape elements and design techniques.

LAUD 202.name: Design Studio II: Housing Environment
LAUD 202.description: Focus on housing as a fundamental component of the urban environment; exploration of housing design across multiple scales through the relationship between dwelling units, open space systems, and the broader urban context; emphasis on the integration of landscape and urban design strategies in shaping livable, inclusive, and context-responsive residential environments.

LAUD 221.name: Introduction to Urban Design
LAUD 221.description: Introduction to urban design as an autonomous discipline with its own theoretical framework, concepts, and tools; examination of analytical, formative, instrumental, and responsive dimensions of urban design; engagement with seminal texts and key theories shaping the discipline and the physical form of cities; establishment of conceptual and theoretical groundwork for subsequent studio and theory courses in the program.

LAUD 232.name: Landscape Representation
LAUD 232.description: This course aims at exploring new ways to interpret, conceive and express landscape by means of different techniques required to develop ideas from the early stages of design projects to the deployment phase. Topics include: "mastering ways of seeing", "strategies of representation", "finding of graphic style", "creating materials and images to show design", and "targeting different presentations".

LAUD 241.name: Landscape Plants
LAUD 241.description: Beginning level lecture and field study course covering basic biological structure of plants, their classification and botanical (Latin) names, plants' visual characteristics, ecological requirements and their design use.

LAUD 242.name: Flora of Turkey
LAUD 242.description: Building a general framework to familiarize students with the variety of Turkey's flora while understanding effects of climate, topography and soil on plant communities.

LAUD 251.name: Introduction to Landscape Theory
LAUD 251.description: An introductory lecture-based course that aims to build a theoretical basis to understand meaning and scope of landscape architecture and urban design, the major components of landscape architecture such as environmental conditions, human factors, landform and landscape elements; topography, vegetation, water and built material.

LAUD 252.name: Environmental Site Design: Landform and Water
LAUD 252.description: Exploration of landforms and water systems as integral components of environmental site design. Introduction to land reading, geomorphology, grading, and contour manipulation. Development of skills in topographic analysis, land surveying, and cut-and-fill calculations. Examination of water-sensitive design approaches, including drainage, stormwater management, and erosion control. Integration of landform and water strategies into context-responsive site design proposals.

LAUD 290.name: Summer Practice II
LAUD 290.description: Summer practice building a familiarity with plant material and their physical properties, to develop a basic understanding about their propagation and maintenance techniques. Carried out in nurseries for a minimum period of 4 weeks.

LAUD 301.name: Design Studio III: Town Center
LAUD 301.description: Focus on the design of town centers as complex, multi-functional urban environments within larger urban systems; examination of the spatial, social, cultural, and political dynamics shaping central areas, with particular attention to core-periphery relationships and processes of transformation and densification; investigation of town centers as nodes of activity, exchange, and identity through site analysis, mapping, and design development; emphasis on multifunctionality, public space systems, density, accessibility, and the integration of transportation networks.

LAUD 302.name: Design Studio IV: Urban Nature
LAUD 302.description: Focus on the regeneration of degraded urban landscapes through ecological and spatial strategies; examination of cities as socio-ecological systems shaped by the interaction of natural and built environments, grounded in urban ecology and nature-based solutions; development of context-sensitive design proposals addressing climate adaptation, resilience, and landscape regeneration through the integration of ecological thinking into spatial design.

LAUD 324.name: Morphology and Topology of Urban Spaces
LAUD 324.description: Discussion and analysis of physical principles, functions, relationships, and physical elements of urban spaces. Various techniques/methods to make a typological and morphological study of urban spaces.

LAUD 342.name: Planting Design Studio
LAUD 342.description: Introduction to planting design and its significance in landscape architecture considering its structural characteristics, visual properties, symbolic meanings, psychological effects and sensual experience.

LAUD 357.name: Landscape Construction: Techniques, Materials and Structures
LAUD 357.description: The aim is of this course is to provide students the basic information about materials and structures used in landscape design, their design potential and limitations, design details and construction methods. Develop creative abilities and skills in project preparation and construction of small forms in civil engineering solutions for the realization of urban environment.

LAUD 362.name: Making of Urban Landscape
LAUD 362.description: A field study oriented elective course aiming to reveal the 'spirit' of the place and everyday life. Survey, analysis, diagnosis and design of the city's components to see and understand the urban form, its elements and related conditions. Public open spaces, squares, clusters of houses, transportation hubs, cultural nodes, recreational areas, etc.

LAUD 372.name: Measuring Urban Form: Morphometrics and Spatial Artificial Intelligence
LAUD 372.description: Introduction to methods for measuring, assessing, and understanding urban form; exploration of qualitative and quantitative techniques including typo-morphology, network analysis, behavior mapping, and introductory machine learning and spatial AI applications; hands-on engagement with analytical tools and concepts in urban morphology through workshop-based study using Ankara as a living laboratory; development of an evidence-based evaluation framework connecting rigorous measurement to design reasoning.

LAUD 390.name: Summer Practice III
LAUD 390.description: Summer practice carried out in two 3-week stages, the first stage focusing on the application of soft material, planting techniques, plant composition and maintenance processes, and the second stage focusing on the application of hard material, in addition to the preparation of bills of quantity and tender documents.

LAUD 401.name: Senior Design Studio I: Urban Systems
LAUD 401.description: Focus on the interrelations of diverse urban systems and subsystems in addressing complex landscape and urban design challenges; examination of the city as a dynamic and continuously transforming entity; exploration of urban complexity through multi-scalar analysis and design development across micro, meso, and macro scales; development of spatially articulated design proposals responding to ongoing urban change; emphasis on systems thinking and data analytics as tools integrated with design processes.

LAUD 402.name: Senior Design Studio II: Graduation Projects
LAUD 402.description: The finale of the Vertical Design Studio System composed of three different studios: Concept, Context and Form in which the second, third and fourth year students are enrolled. Urban design and landscape architecture medium of knowledge gained through the undergraduate education via special topics in selected cities.

LAUD 404.name: Senior Design Research
LAUD 404.description: A seminar format research course to provide a knowledge basis for the Senior Design Studio, and prepare students for a variety of professional careers. Enhancement of skills of critical and analytical thinking and creative problem solving while developing social awareness.

LAUD 417.name: Contract Documents
LAUD 417.description: A lecture/studio course studying the technical and practical aspects of organizing the components of a full set of contract documents for a landscape and urban design project. All working drawings, bills of quantity, organization of the specifications and relationship of these components to the conditions of tender and contract prepared and compiled in a portfolio.

LAUD 418.name: Professional Practice and Ethics
LAUD 418.description: Professional practice in landscape architecture; social, legal, ethical, technical, and financial dimensions. Design process and management; project coordination and implementation. Roles, responsibilities, and ethical conduct in relation to clients, contractors, and the public. Office management, contracting procedures, and project supervision. Analysis of professional documents and application-based project work.

LAUD 421.name: Realization of Urban Projects
LAUD 421.description: This is an interactive course, studying the conditions/factors, partners/actors, elements of project realizations, to provide better urban environments. During the course, problems that may be encountered at different levels of urban project realization in terms of legal, institutional, financial issues will be taken up. Various approaches to urban problems will be discussed with the students and the students will be exposed to different case studies given by guest lectures.

LAUD 422.name: Processing Urban Design Competitions
LAUD 422.description: The conceptual and discursive background of national and international urban design competitions from the past to the present will be discussed. Along with the competition processes, there will be discussions on how this process is described from the perspective of both the employer and the competitors. Designers who participated in urban design competitions and received awards will be invited to present their projects and processes. The course aims at equipping students of architecture, urban design and landscape architecture with necessary skills to excel in urban design competitions.

LAUD 461.name: Occupancy in Urban Areas
LAUD 461.description: Relationship between people and the physical settings, particularly urban public spaces. Field studies to analyze cases in different contexts.

LAUD 466.name: Designing the Sustainable City
LAUD 466.description: This course aims to develop a critical understanding of Sustainable Urban Design (SUD) by looking at the complex human-nature relationship and the environmental consequences caused by this interaction. Students will explore the current issues through analyzing best practices addressing different aspects of SUD at different geographic scales. Students will learn the basic principles to perform analysis using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) tools. They will also examine the role of different actors and institutions in decision-making process, the efforts in formulating guiding principles and action plans to achieve sustainable cities. Through a term project, students will have the opportunity to apply the sustainable practices they learned in the class with the use of GIS mapping software. In the scope of the term project, they will prepare a SUD guideline including objectives, policies and programs to assist future urban development.

LAUD 471.name: City, Culture and Society
LAUD 471.description: A critical introduction to the social and cultural dimensions of urban life through the examination of the city as a site of power, identity, conflict, and transformation; engagement with contemporary theoretical frameworks and pressing urban issues including inequality, displacement, climate change, and digital transformation; development of analytical tools for critically assessing the social production of the built environment and its implications for urban design and landscape architecture practice.

LAUD 472.name: Recent Issues in Human Geography
LAUD 472.description: Relations between society, space and social science in a changing world. Recent approaches in analyzing the relationships between society and space in different time and space contexts with an emphasis on time-space geography, agency and structure relationships, local/global dynamics, images and symbols in different cultural contexts.

LAUD 473.name: Experiencing the City
LAUD 473.description: Human experience in various urban settings focusing on the nature of private and public spaces. Analysis of spatial and social factors that define the context of urban life and experience with selected cases.

LAUD 474.name: Space, Culture and Identity
LAUD 474.description: Cultural and political contradictions of urban design. Urban design turning the city into a scientific object of knowledge, a laboratorium of modernity, and a site for the formation of new experiences and identities. Cases of urban design and its politics, historically and theoretically, from different places across the globe.

LAUD 475.name: Cinema and Space
LAUD 475.description: Multiple readings of interior and exterior spaces within the framework of the theory of cinematic montage and cinematic imagery. An analogy between cinema and space design, and the eye and the camera. Design as a cinematographic process. Both creative acts are organized in time through space and perceived through time in space.

LAUD 476.name: Visual Politics of Space
LAUD 476.description: The relation between systems of visual representation and social power relations through the connection(s) between image and space. The capacity of visual representations to produce meaning, the political implications of such meanings, and the social functions of these representations in an interval between the mid-19th century to the end of the 20th century. The role of various visual media (painting, photography, cinema) on the ways of perceiving, conceptualizing and socially defining space.

LAUD 481.name: Climate Justice & Ecological Design
LAUD 481.description: Climate crisis as a framework for ecological design in landscape architecture and urban design. Examination of ecosystems, environmental limits, and climate risks across multiple scales.Climate change as a socio-ecological challenge shaped by inequality, vulnerability, and environmental injustice. Development of mitigation, adaptation, and regenerative design strategies. Integration of site-based research, analysis, and design to produce resilient, contextresponsive ecological proposals.

LAUD 483.name: Environment Philosophy and Ethics
LAUD 483.description: The meaning of environment and human attitude towards nature and other living things. Related environmental topics and issues in the light of environmental philosophy and ethics. Students from a variety of disciplines building a certain level of consciousness, responsibility and skills to understand and resolve environmental conflicts.
